### Definitions and Differences

* **Machine:** A combination of resistant bodies configured to transform available energy into useful mechanical work or motion (e.g., Lathe machine, internal combustion engine).
* **Mechanism:** A system of rigid bodies connected by joints to transform motion into a prescribed output motion without necessarily transmitting significant power (e.g., Slider-crank mechanism, four-bar chain).

#### Difference Between Machine and Mechanism:

| Feature | Machine | Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Function** | Transmits power and performs useful work. | Only transforms or transmits motion. |
| **Energy** | Consumes and transforms energy. | Does not necessarily deal with power/energy. |
| **Components** | Contains mechanisms as its parts. | Consists of links and joints. |
proTip: Remember: All machines are mechanisms, but not all mechanisms are machines.
